claims.text: Calling `toString` on a Pulumi `Output<T>` yields the placeholder text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` instead of the resolved value.

The placeholder text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` can show up in a log line, a generated file, or a resource property when a Pulumi output is treated as if it were already a plain value.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and covers this symptom and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers diagnosing errors that arise from stringifying an output value, branching on an output value, or reading an output value as if it were a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, stringifying an output value, branching on it (e.g., in a conditional), or reading it like a plain value produces errors, because outputs are not plain values at program run time.

Pulumi produces a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when a stack already has an update running, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists to address it.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/ exists to address them.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/ exists and covers post-step event failures and engine bugs in Pulumi.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/ exists and covers network connectivity and proxy problems with Pulumi.

The Pulumi CLI emits a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, and the page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/ has an anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml that addresses it.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ exists and covers scenarios where `pulumi destroy` fails.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/ exists and covers recovering from interrupted Pulumi deployments.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 Pulumi binaries under Rosetta 2 causes crashes or hangs, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/architecture-mismatch/ exists to address this.
The page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/ exists and covers resolving continuous integration and deployment pipeline issues with Pulumi.
The page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/ exists and describes safe techniques for modifying Pulumi state files.
A recently deleted Pulumi stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
The Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources, which can help when a stuck or misbehaving resource blocks a wider update.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics, documented at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/.
Pulumi offers pre-release dev builds that can be installed to access bug fixes that have not yet shipped in a stable release.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed Pulumi operation to the Pulumi team, and the logging guide has an anchor #automatic-logging describing this.
The `pulumi logs share` command exists in the Pulumi CLI.
Pulumi has a Community Slack reachable at https://slack.pulumi.com that provides community support.
A guide for filing GitHub issues exists at /docs/support/filing-issues/ explaining how to report bugs in the right repository.
Pulumi offers paid support options, reachable via the /contact/ page.
Navigating to the troubleshooting page with the #conflict hash redirects to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/, tracked in pulumi/pulumi issue 20846.

Navigating to the troubleshooting page with the #verbose-logging hash redirects to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging, tracked in pulumi/docs issue 16985; the #cli-verbose-logging anchor exists on the logging page.
The troubleshooting section provides comprehensive troubleshooting guides for common issues with Pulumi infrastructure, deployments, and configuration.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.

The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs exists and covers Outputs; /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ ("Accessing single outputs with Apply") and /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/ ("Working with multiple outputs") exist.

When an output value is concatenated, logged, or otherwise converted to a string directly (without apply or an equivalent helper), Pulumi does not raise an error by default and instead silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In Pulumi TypeScript, converting an Output to a string via template literal yields a string containing the literal text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.

In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value, and no exception is thrown.
In Pulumi Python, formatting an Output into an f-string yields a string containing the literal text `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and no exception is raised.
In Pulumi Python, converting an Output to a string via __str__ also logs a warning.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` is the alternative to use.
Pulumi Python provides `Output.json_dumps()` for serializing outputs to JSON.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a plain `string` is expected is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise.
In Pulumi Go, output values are resolved inside `ApplyT`.

In Pulumi C#, converting an Output to a string via string interpolation yields a string containing the literal text `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`, and no exception is thrown.

Because the placeholder mistake doesn't throw, the program runs and `pulumi up` succeeds, and the placeholder text only surfaces later in a log line, generated config file, or downstream resource property.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes converting an Output to a string throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning the placeholder text.
The `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING` environment variable is supported in the TypeScript, Python, and C# Pulumi SDKs (but not Go).
`pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` are the string-composition helpers for Outputs in the Pulumi TypeScript SDK.
`Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` are the string-composition helpers for Outputs in the Pulumi Python SDK.
`pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` are the string-composition helpers for Outputs in the Pulumi Go SDK.
`Output.Format` is the string-composition helper for Outputs in the Pulumi C# SDK.

A value read from an Output inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in another output derived from it); assigning it to an outer variable and using it outside the callback does not work.

The Pulumi `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, which is in general after the program's top-level code has already finished running, so reading an outer variable assigned in the callback yields `undefined`.
The `apply` callback runs when the Pulumi engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix the ordering problem.
Passing an Output directly as an input to another resource (e.g., `bucket: bucket.bucketName` on `aws.s3.BucketObject`) lets Pulumi resolve the dependency without needing `apply`.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values.
A handful of positions in a Pulumi program, such as a resource's logical name, cannot accept an Output.

In a dynamically typed Pulumi language, an `if` statement on an Output evaluates the Output object rather than its eventual value, so the condition is generally always true regardless of what the output resolves to.
In a statically typed Pulumi language, branching on an Output is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.

A value known when the program starts — such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag — is a plain value and can be branched on normally.
When a branch depends on a resource's output, the branch must move inside `apply`, deriving a new Output whose value depends on the branch.

Because branches on outputs can't be expressed as separate blocks of resource-creation code, a runtime branch on an output usually requires restructuring the program so both sets of resources are described unconditionally, or branching on a plain config value instead.

A resource's logical name (the first constructor argument) and loop bounds or map keys used while authoring a Pulumi program must be known plain values while the program is being evaluated, before any resource exists.
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name, loop bound, or map key fails to compile in Pulumi TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Pulumi Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the Output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

When resource names or counts must depend on data only known after a resource is created, one fix is to provision dependent resources in a later, separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a `StackReference`.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/ has a `#stackreferences` section describing StackReference.
Trying to `await` a Pulumi Output or read its value synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or quietly returns placeholder text instead of the value.
Pulumi has no supported way to block the program and pull a resolved value out of an Output synchronously.

Pulumi does not allow synchronously reading outputs because the engine would need the value before it has finished determining the order in which to create resources, defeating the up-front dependency graph.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A `StackReference` in another Pulumi program consumes one stack's outputs as another stack's inputs.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go), usable when driving deployments programmatically.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/ exists and covers the Automation API.

`pulumi stack output`, `StackReference`, and the Automation API outputs field all read a value that has already resolved, rather than unwrapping an in-flight output inside the program that created it.
